clue.text: Sponsors of top criminals

explanation.surface: A question about who backs the leaders of organised crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Godparents sponsor a child at baptism, and Mafia bosses are called by the same title, as in the famous film.

clue.text: Starts to get out the Hunnish invader

indicators.note: the starts of the following words means taking the opening letter of each one

explanation.surface: Beginning to drive off a barbarian attacker like the Huns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunnish invader' reads as one phrase, but Hunnish only gives its H; the Goths were a separate Germanic people who, like the Huns, attacked Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were a Germanic people who overran parts of the Roman Empire, so one of them was an invader.

clue.text: Instruction to take no action about Sandhurst is inoperative

indicators.note: about means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: a curt 'don't' tells someone to refrain from doing anything
RMA, the Royal Military Academy, is at Sandhurst in Berkshire

explanation.surface: An order to halt activity at the military academy has stopped everything there.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer training college, the Royal Military Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is asleep or inactive, not currently working.

clue.text: Everything satisfactory — but still arrange to move

indicators.note: to move tells us the letters of the two words before it shift position

explanation.surface: All seems well, yet someone still wants to organise a house move.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is old British slang from Victorian times, after General Sir Garnet Wolseley, famed for efficient campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian expression means that all is in order, a catchphrase for things being just right.

clue.text: Conceal, say, an explorer in London

indicators.note: say signals that the word for conceal is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to conceal something is to hide it
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the River Niger

explanation.surface: Hide, as it were, a famous adventurer somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just a location: the answer is a large royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the best-known royal parks, lying in the west of the capital.

clue.text: Top missing from iron tripods — bolts needed

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: trivets are three-legged iron stands for pots by a fire

explanation.surface: A pot stand has lost its upper part and needs fixing with metal pins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top missing from' takes the T off TRIVETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivets are metal pins used as fasteners, broadly a kind of bolt.

clue.text: Plant goddess

explanation.surface: A spy planting a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is saltwort, a seaside herb; the second is the Hindu deity of time and destruction.

clue.text: A row outside the Spanish workshop

indicators.note: outside means the word for row goes round the Spanish article

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An argument erupts outside a factory in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but is a line of seats, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's studio or craftsman's workroom.

clue.text: Effects of tools

explanation.surface: The belongings left behind by some tools.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means carries out or puts into practice; as a noun it means instruments or utensils.

clue.text: Siamese creatures for a loving person

definitions.meaning: Siamese twins are joined, and these birds are proverbially inseparable pairs
an affectionate sweetheart, from the birds' devoted pairing

explanation.surface: Thai animals as a symbol for someone affectionate.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds are emblems of faithful love, always seen in devoted pairs, hence a pet name for a sweetheart.

clue.text: Hang on to the tower

explanation.surface: Holding on to a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain is the verb sense; the noun is the strongest central tower of a castle.

clue.text: Articles about kind of light — that's just what I was wanting

definitions.text: that's just what I was wanting

indicators.note: about means these two words wrap around the flare

parts.note: the definite article and a thing (an article, an object) together
a Very light is a coloured signal flare fired from a pistol

explanation.surface: Someone finds newspaper pieces on a type of lamp exactly what they needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' gives two pieces: THE, a grammatical article, and THING, an article in the sense of an object.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something exactly suited to a need.

clue.text: Scholar and soldier are Zoroastrians

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a degree held by a scholar
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: An academic and a soldier both follow an ancient Persian religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men of the Nativity were priests of the ancient Persian faith of Zoroaster.

clue.text: It gives singers a note to get black hose

parts.note: pitch-black, so pitch means black
a hose is a pipe for water

explanation.surface: A choirmaster's tuning aid, apparently obtained by getting a dark hosepipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reed pipe blown to sound the starting tone for a choir.

clue.text: Bill is on the ball, accepting the book agreement

indicators.note: accepting means the pair of pieces takes the book inside it
in a down clue, being on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a ball is a formal dance
Cor is the abbreviation for Corinthians, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill is alert and goes along with a published deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the ball' looks like the idiom for alert, but 'is on' simply sets AC above DANCE, and 'accepting' takes COR into that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord means being in agreement or conformity, as in the phrase in accordance with.

clue.text: Type of grey coat perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be ordered otherwise

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of overcoat is in grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or kind of thing.

clue.text: Opposed to States English

parts.note: avers means declares or states

explanation.surface: Being against the United States of English speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' reads as the nations but is the verb, AVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be averse is to be disinclined or hostile, set against something.

clue.text: Rebuke fish salesman first

indicators.note: first means the salesman comes before the fish

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Scold the fishmonger before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach is to scold or criticise someone.

clue.text: Protest at umpire's announcement

parts.note: the cricket umpire's verdict when a batsman is dismissed
a cry is a public call, as by a town crier

explanation.surface: Complaints about a decision called by an umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Umpire's' gives the word an umpire calls to dismiss a batsman, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public objection.

clue.text: River goddess is willing

parts.note: the Test is a trout river in Hampshire
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: A water deity says she is ready to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' means having made a will, not keen. The Test is a river in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes someone who died having made a legal will, so humorously one who is will-ing.

clue.text: It is on credit in the main — and worn out

indicators.note: in an across clue, being on means placed after the other part
in means the credit abbreviation is put inside the sea

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea, the deep
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Money banked at sea is old and battered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like a main road or principal thing, but it is the old word for the open sea; 'is on' places the final pronoun after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means weakened by age or use, falling apart.

clue.text: Settler puts money on two aces with a little hesitation

parts.note: p, penny or pence, a small unit of money
an ace is a one, here written as the Roman numeral
the second ace is written out as the word for 1
er is a short pause in speech

explanation.surface: A frontiersman hesitantly bets cash on a pair of aces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two aces' gives the figure 1 two ways: the Roman numeral I and the word ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first people to settle a new territory.

clue.text: Make impertinent inquiry about worker in food store

indicators.note: about means the word for nosy inquiry goes round the worker

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy
a worker ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Nosing around after an employee at the grocery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a cupboard or small room where food is kept.

clue.text: Rapid rise, sadly, in dilapidation.

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words have gone badly wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building's swift ascent unhappily ends in ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is the state of having fallen into decay through neglect.

clue.text: Play about king in Asia Minor

indicators.note: about means the word for play wraps round the king

parts.note: to toy with is to play
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A drama concerning a monarch set in Anatolia.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a location: the ancient city of the Trojan War stood in what is now Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city besieged by the Greeks lay in northwest Anatolia.

clue.text: Island with little relation to the Thames

parts.note: sis, short for sister

explanation.surface: An island linked to the London river.
explanation.walkthrough: The river Thames is called the Isis where it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford calls its stretch of the great river by this local name.

clue.text: Expression of joy on coming back to Arkwright

indicators.note: coming back means the little word on is read in reverse

parts.note: ah is an exclamation of pleasure

explanation.surface: A cheer of delight on returning to a mill pioneer's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arkwright' suggests Richard Arkwright, inventor of the spinning frame, but means one who built an ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A wright is a builder, and the Biblical patriarch built the ark before the Flood.

clue.text: Side sent as replacement to give stability

indicators.note: replacement means the letters are put back in new places

explanation.surface: A substitute team is fielded to bring calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness is firmness and balance, not wavering.

clue.text: Statesman in paradise

explanation.surface: A politician in heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden was British prime minister in the 1950s; the garden where Adam and Eve lived is the Biblical paradise.

clue.text: A quiet story, maybe about an ugly old woman and a Greek

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the old woman
maybe shows the letters could be ordered another way

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken tale concerning a crone and a Hellenic man.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'maybe' anagram uses the clue's opening A and the P for quiet along with the story, making PYTORAS; 'about' wraps that round the crone after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous mathematician and philosopher came from Samos in ancient Greece.
